what: float64 second-order operators with state-dependent diagonal diffusion sum_i s_i(x)^2 d^2 u / dx_i^2 of deep tanh MLPs u(t, x) = wo . tanh(W_L ... tanh(W_1 (t, x) + b_1) ...) + bo, W_1 of shape (H, 1 + D), at B points (t ~ U(0, 1), x ~ N(0, I)): forward = operator values; vg = 0.5 mean (Op u - f)^2 and its gradient w.r.t. every weight, bias and readout parameter. Candidate = omnibias.jax.experimental.projected_laplacian.projected_deep_laplacian with point_diffusion = s(x_b) per point and the drift (1, v(x_b)) as a carried first-order direction: per point G_b = M diag(s_b^2) M^T (M the space columns of W_1; one packed product over the H (H + 1) / 2 row pairs when 2 B >= H, a batched product otherwise) and a batched H x H Cholesky factor, so the hidden recursion carries k = min(D, H) columns. The cell with D < H is a control where the projection cannot reduce anything; the previous-interface tier is the same module without point_diffusion, vmapped over points with a shared diagonal per call (under vmap its fallback conditional runs both branches); the projected-generic tier feeds the same per-point projected columns to generic engines, isolating the closed-form recursion from the projection; nested autodiff runs where D <= 1024
hardware: one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (exclusive), JAX 0.10.2 with jaxlib 0.10.2 CUDA 12 plugins, CPython 3.12

protocol.repetitions: 3 fresh processes (paired by repetition, rotating method order)
protocol.statistic: ratio = strongest-control median / candidate median per tier; lower95 = exp(mean(log r) - 2.920 sd(log r)/sqrt(3)); strongest control = smallest mean log median among qualified tier members
protocol.qualification: every method's forward and vg programs on a reduced instance (width 4, D_q = min(D, 40) > 4 space coordinates so the per-point projection is active, B = 2 or 1 so the full-size Gram path is the one qualified, seed + 1) vs a 50-digit oracle (second-order Taylor series over (t, x) along every scaled space direction plus the drift, no projection; objective derivatives along two fixed random parameter directions by central differences in 50 digits): values and objective 1e-9 / 2e-10, directional derivatives 1e-8 / 2e-9 (scaled); full-size outputs finite and digest-checked

status.parity: lower95 < 1 <= ratio or ratio < 1 <= upper bound
status.partial: an applicable tier member failed (e.g. out of memory) or did not qualify; never promoted

protocol.fairness: identical data, initialisation, loss and float64 inputs for every method; compilation excluded (value-and-gradient steady state)

tiers.previous_interface: the same module without point_diffusion, vmapped over points with diffusion = s_b and directions = v_b: one shared-diagonal call per point
tiers.forward_laplacian_full_seed: the same recursion seeded per point with W_1[:, 1:] diag(s_b); equal to collapsed Taylor mode for this operator; omnibias.jax.laplacian.deep_field_value_grad_laplacian and folx.forward_laplacian of y -> u(t, s_b y) at y = x / s_b, vmapped over points
tiers.taylor_mode: jax.experimental.jet, one second-order jet per scaled space column per point, started at the first pre-activation
tiers.projected_generic: the same per-point projection with generic engines: jet with the k = min(D, H) columns F_b of the independent program, and folx.forward_laplacian of y -> u at z_1 + F_b y; isolates the closed-form recursion from the projection
tiers.nested_autodiff: jax.hessian over (t, x) per point and the s_b^2-weighted space diagonal; D <= 1024

roles.held_out: cells, operators and seed not used for any tuning

full_size_accuracy.what: max over repetitions of per-field relative deviations (norms and sampled entries scaled by the largest sampled reference magnitude) between methods at full size; floor = two controls

cold_cost.what: per cell, medians over repetitions: cold = lowering + compilation ms (excluded from the speed ratios), steady = steady-state median ms, for the candidate and the steady-state-fastest member of every tier; break_even_calls = extra cold ms / steady saving per call (only when the candidate compiles slower and runs faster)
